Oh really? I didn't have an issue with their culturing tbh. Just wrt their markers. I'm only talking about microglia here. It's very difficult to get their exclusive markers. We tried so many methods then. Embryoid bodies (EBs) and then flow cytometry (FC), fixing those EBs, using surface markers, and then nuclear markers, using staining instead of FC etc. The issue is that the project (obviously) involved a double-marker study so the gating was very difficult in FC and on the microscope after the immunocytochemistry, it was the same thing. Coz you needed two markers to be expressed above a certain threshold to confirm the identity of the cell type
Just to give a disclaimer: that project didn't involve basic research. It was somewhere between basic research and translational research. So confirming the identity of the cells at every stage was foundational
